question.worked_solution:
To find the roots of $f(x),$ we must solve $f(x)=0:$

$$
\sqrt[4]{3x+15}-3=0
$$

We solve this equation by making $x$ the subject, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt[4]{3x+15}-3 & =0 \\ \sqrt[4]{3x+15} & =3 \\ (\sqrt[4]{3x+15})^{4} & ={3}^{4} \\ 3x+15 & =81 \\ 3x & =66 \\ x & =22\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we must check the answer by substituting it back into the initial equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt[4]{3\cdot 22+15}-3 & =0 \\ \sqrt[4]{81}-3 & =0 \\ 0 & =0\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the root of $f(x)$ is $x=22.$
